title: Anthropic expands Claude's context window to 100K tokens
whatChanged: Anthropic raised Claude's context window from 9K to 100K tokens, about 75,000 words.
whyCare: Teams could put whole documents into one prompt for the first time at this scale.
before: Most models held a few thousand tokens, so long documents had to be split or summarised first.
after: A single request could hold a long report, contract or codebase section.
learn: Compare long context with retrieval on your own documents. Measure cost and accuracy for each.

sources.name: Anthropic - Introducing 100K context windows

architectureImplication: Long context became a design option next to retrieval. Choose per use case based on cost, latency and accuracy.

title: Meta releases Llama 2 free for research and commercial use
whatChanged: Meta released Llama 2 with model weights that companies could download and use commercially, together with Microsoft as a launch partner.
whyCare: Companies could run a capable model on their own infrastructure under a license that allowed business use.
before: Strong models were mostly available only through hosted APIs, and open models were limited or research-only.
after: Teams could self-host, fine-tune and control a capable model.
learn: Check the license terms for your use case. Plan for hosting, updates and safety controls you now own.

sources.name: Meta - Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama

architectureImplication: Self-hosted models became a real option for data control and cost. Teams take on serving, scaling and model updates.

title: OWASP publishes the first Top 10 risks for LLM applications
whatChanged: OWASP published version 1.0 of its Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, a list of the main security risks such as prompt injection and insecure output handling.
whyCare: Security teams got a shared list to review LLM applications against.
before: Teams had no common reference for LLM-specific security risks.
after: Reviews, threat models and vendor questionnaires could point to one public list.
learn: Review your application against the current version of the list. Add the relevant risks to your threat model.

sources.name: OWASP - Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
SD Times - OWASP releases Top 10 list for LLMs

architectureImplication: Treat model input and output as untrusted. Add controls for prompt injection, output handling and excessive agent permissions.
verificationNote: The OWASP page shows no release date. Date from SD Times coverage published 2 August 2023.

title: Microsoft makes Microsoft 365 Copilot generally available to enterprises
whatChanged: Microsoft made Copilot for Microsoft 365 generally available to enterprise customers on 1 November 2023, inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams.
whyCare: GenAI moved into the office software most companies already use, with access tied to existing company data and permissions.
before: Most GenAI use at work happened in separate chat tools.
after: Employees could use GenAI inside their daily applications, grounded in company files and email.
learn: Check how your data permissions apply when an assistant can read across files and email. Fix oversharing before rollout.

sources.name: Microsoft - Announcing Microsoft 365 Copilot general availability and Microsoft 365 Chat

architectureImplication: Existing access controls became the boundary for what AI can see. Data governance became a prerequisite for rollout.

title: OpenAI launches the Assistants API and GPT-4 Turbo with 128K context
whatChanged: At DevDay, OpenAI announced GPT-4 Turbo with a 128K context window, JSON mode, and the Assistants API with threads, retrieval and code execution.
whyCare: Developers could build assistants that keep state and use tools without running that infrastructure themselves.
before: Developers stored conversation state, retrieval and tool loops in their own code.
after: The platform could hold threads, files and tool calls for them.
learn: Decide which state you want the vendor to hold. Check how to export it if you change vendors.

sources.name: OpenAI - New models and developer products announced at DevDay

architectureImplication: State and tool orchestration could move into the vendor platform. This trades build effort for portability.

title: The EU AI Act enters into force
whatChanged: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. Its rules apply in stages over the following years.
whyCare: Teams that build or use AI in the EU now have legal duties that depend on the risk level of each use case.
before: No broad law set rules for how AI systems are built and used in the EU.
after: Providers and deployers must classify use cases by risk and meet the duties for each level.
learn: List your AI use cases and classify them by risk. Track which obligations apply on which date.

sources.name: European Commission - AI Act enters into force

architectureImplication: Plan for documentation, logging, human oversight and transparency features as part of the design.

title: OpenAI makes model output follow a developer's JSON schema
whatChanged: OpenAI introduced Structured Outputs in the API. Model outputs now reliably follow a JSON Schema the developer supplies.
whyCare: Systems that pass model output to other code can rely on its shape.
before: Developers asked for JSON in the prompt, then validated and retried when the output broke.
after: The API guarantees the output matches the schema.
learn: Define schemas for every model output that other code reads. Remove retry logic that only fixed format errors.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing Structured Outputs in the API

architectureImplication: Model output can feed other systems directly. Validation still matters for content, though format errors drop away.

title: Anthropic introduces prompt caching for long, repeated context
whatChanged: Anthropic launched prompt caching for Claude. Reusing a cached prompt prefix cuts cost by up to 90% and latency by up to 85% for long prompts.
whyCare: Long system prompts, documents and tool definitions became cheap to resend on every call.
before: Every request paid full price for the whole prompt, even when most of it repeated.
after: Repeated context costs a fraction of the normal input price.
learn: Put stable content at the start of the prompt and changing content at the end. Measure your cache hit rate.

sources.name: Anthropic - Prompt caching with Claude
SD Times - Anthropic introduces prompt caching

architectureImplication: Prompt structure became a cost lever. Agents and long-context designs got much cheaper to run.
verificationNote: Anthropic's page now shows a later republish date. Launch date confirmed by news coverage from 14 August 2024.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Code, an agentic coding tool for the terminal
whatChanged: Anthropic released Claude Code in limited research preview with Claude 3.7 Sonnet. Developers can hand off engineering tasks from their terminal.
whyCare: Coding assistants started to act on a codebase, editing files and running commands.
before: Coding assistants mostly suggested code inside an editor for a developer to accept.
after: An agent could carry out multi-step engineering tasks under a developer's direction.
learn: Set clear permissions for what a coding agent may run. Review its changes like any other contributor's.

sources.name: Anthropic - Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code

architectureImplication: Developer machines and repositories became places where agents act. Permissions and review gates matter.

title: OpenAI launches Codex, a cloud coding agent that works on tasks in parallel
whatChanged: OpenAI introduced Codex as a cloud-based software engineering agent that can work on many tasks in parallel.
whyCare: Coding agents moved off the developer's machine and into managed cloud sandboxes.
before: Coding agents ran one task at a time on a developer's machine.
after: Teams could queue several coding tasks to agents running in the cloud.
learn: Decide which repositories and secrets a cloud agent may access. Track the cost and quality of agent work.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing Codex

architectureImplication: Agent work became something you can run in parallel and in the cloud. Sandboxes, secrets and review queues became part of the design.

title: EU AI Act rules for general-purpose AI models start to apply
whatChanged: From 2 August 2025, providers of general-purpose AI models in the EU must meet transparency and copyright duties under the AI Act.
whyCare: Model providers must now document their models, which gives teams more information when they choose one.
before: Model providers had no legal duty in the EU to document training data or model capabilities.
after: Providers must publish documentation and a summary of training content.
learn: Ask model vendors for their AI Act documentation. Use it in your model selection and risk records.

sources.name: European Commission - General-purpose AI obligations under the AI Act

architectureImplication: Vendor documentation becomes an input to model selection and compliance records.

title: OpenAI releases gpt-oss, its first open-weight models since 2019
whatChanged: OpenAI released gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b under the Apache 2.0 license.
whyCare: A leading model lab now offered open weights, so teams could self-host models from the same vendor they use through an API.
before: OpenAI models were available only through hosted services.
after: Teams could run OpenAI reasoning models on their own infrastructure.
learn: Test the open models against your hosted model on the same tasks. Compare total cost, including serving.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing gpt-oss

architectureImplication: Mixed designs became easier: hosted models for some tasks, self-hosted open weights for sensitive or high-volume ones.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5 with a router between fast and deep reasoning
whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-5 as the new default in ChatGPT. A router picks a quick model or a deeper reasoning model for each request.
whyCare: Choosing between a fast model and a reasoning model became something the system can decide per request.
before: Users and developers picked a reasoning or non-reasoning model themselves.
after: One entry point routes each request to the right level of reasoning.
learn: Test how routing affects your cost and latency. Pin a model version where you need predictable behaviour.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing GPT-5

architectureImplication: Routing between model tiers became a standard design pattern, inside vendor products and in your own systems.

title: Anthropic adds context editing and a memory tool for long-running agents
whatChanged: Anthropic launched context editing, which clears stale tool results as the context fills, and a memory tool that stores information in files outside the context. OpenAI added compaction in December 2025 and Anthropic a Compaction API in February 2026.
whyCare: Agents can now run far longer than one context window because the platform manages what stays in context.
before: Developers trimmed, summarised and stored agent context with their own code.
after: Major platforms offer context editing, memory and compaction as built-in features.
learn: Test how your agent behaves when old context is cleared or compacted. Decide what must go to durable memory.

sources.name: Anthropic - Managing context on the Claude Developer Platform
OpenAI - API changelog (compaction, 11 December 2025)
Anthropic - Claude Platform release notes (Compaction API, 5 February 2026)

architectureImplication: Context became a managed resource. Design what lives in the window, what goes to memory and what gets summarised.

title: Linux Foundation forms the Agentic AI Foundation for MCP, goose and AGENTS.md
whatChanged: The Linux Foundation announced the Agentic AI Foundation, with the Model Context Protocol, goose and AGENTS.md as founding projects.
whyCare: Key agent standards moved under neutral governance, which lowers the risk of building on them.
before: MCP and related agent standards were led by single companies.
learn: Prefer standards with neutral governance for long-lived integrations. Track the foundation's specification releases.

sources.name: Linux Foundation - Announces the formation of the Agentic AI Foundation

architectureImplication: MCP-based integrations became a safer long-term bet for tool and data connections.

title: Anthropic publishes Agent Skills as an open standard
whatChanged: Anthropic published the Agent Skills specification as an open standard at agentskills.io. OpenAI added Skills support to its Responses API in February 2026.
whyCare: Teams can package instructions, scripts and resources for agents once and use them across vendors.
before: Each agent platform had its own way to package reusable know-how.
after: A shared format works across at least two major platforms.
learn: Package repeated agent procedures as skills. Keep them in version control like code.

sources.name: Anthropic - Organization skills and directory
OpenAI - API changelog (Skills in the Responses API, 10 February 2026)

architectureImplication: Agent know-how became a portable asset that teams can version, review and share.

title: EU AI Act transparency rules start to apply
whatChanged: From 2 August 2026, AI-generated content such as deepfakes must be labelled, and users must be told when they interact with an AI system such as a chatbot.
whyCare: Customer-facing AI in the EU now needs disclosure and content labelling built in.
before: Disclosure and labelling were voluntary in most products.
after: Providers and deployers in the EU must disclose AI interaction and label AI-generated content.
learn: Check every customer-facing AI feature for disclosure. Add labels or metadata to generated media.

sources.name: European Commission - Safer and more transparent AI

architectureImplication: Disclosure and content labelling became product requirements for AI features used in the EU.
